title: How many fold lines do these three figures have?
description: A spiky ring, a flower of six curved petals and a looped design with a small square in the centre are folded in the mind. The matching folds of each are counted. Keeko doubts that six petals give six lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: parts that merely repeat round a centre do not make a line of symmetry unless a fold matches them exactly. Watch for students who count petals instead of testing folds.

source: Find all the lines of symmetry of each of three figures: a red outline ring with spiky triangular points, a yellow flower of six curved petals, a green looped design with four round loops and a small square in the centre.
video_script.why: The child tests folds on three figures and learns that repeating parts do not guarantee a line of symmetry.
video_script.substitution: Fold each figure in the mind along straight, across and slanted lines and count the folds where both halves match.
video_script.anchor: Three figures: a red spiky ring, a yellow flower of six curved petals and a green looped design with a small square in the centre
video_script.wrong_answer: the flower with six petals has six lines of symmetry
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the flower has six lines because it has six petals. Folding along a petal puts a petal that curves one way on a petal that curves the other way, so the idea is struck out.
video_script.payoff_line: Parts that only turn round never make a line of symmetry.

final_answer.value: spiky ring: 6 lines; six petal flower: none; looped design: 4 lines
final_answer.spoken: the spiky ring has six lines, the six petal flower has none, and the looped design has four lines

never_show: the counts before the folds are tried
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
The spiky ring has six lines of symmetry.
The flower of six curved petals has no line of symmetry: its petals all curve the same way round, so a fold never matches them.
The looped design has four lines: straight down, straight across and the two corner to corner folds.
Check: fold along each counted line once more.
video_script.design: One idea: count only the folds that match exactly. Assumes the child knows the fold test. The three figures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
open_questions: The book text says all three figures have multiple lines of symmetry, but the worklist gives the six curved petal flower no line of symmetry. This script follows the worklist, because curved petals all turning the same way never fold onto each other. Please confirm against the printed figure.
